distractors.reason: 'Look for' means searching for something that is not yet found. We don't use it when we simply watch something visible like stars.
'Look into' means investigate a problem or question. It is not used for watching the sky.
'Look over' means check something quickly or examine a document. It doesn't describe watching stars.

example_sentence: Every night, astronomers look ___ the stars through powerful telescopes.
l1_interference: Türkçe konuşanlar 'bakmak' fiilinin yönelme hâli ('-e') ekini doğrudan bir edatla eşleştirip 'look to the stars' gibi yanlış yapılar kurabilir. Oysa İngilizcede doğru yapı 'look at'tir.
explanation: In English, 'look at' is used when you direct your eyes toward something you can see. The preposition 'at' points your attention to a specific object.

related_collocations.example: Astronomers look for new planets every year.
Scientists look into the causes of the problem.
I look up the meaning of new words in my dictionary.

memory_tip: LOOK AT = point your eyes at something visible | LOOK FOR = search for something | LOOK INTO = investigate
